crops.name: Almonds
crops.byproducts: Hulls → dairy feed; shells → bedding and soil uses; orchard biomass → soil recycling and energy pathways.

crops.name: Pistachios
crops.byproducts: Shells → farm-road surfacing; some processors compost hulls, leaves and branches; higher-value residue uses remain R&D.

crops.name: Walnuts
crops.byproducts: Shells are a major separated processing stream; USDA is developing shell-based activated carbon and the Walnut Board funds additional byproduct R&D.

CA.role: The center of U.S. tree-nut agriculture. In 2024, almonds and pistachios alone represented 12.6% of all California farm cash receipts.
CA.ecosystem: Mediterranean Central Valley orchards: winter chill, dry summers, managed irrigation, massive pollination logistics, processors and export corridors.

crops.name: Peanuts
crops.byproducts: Shelling creates shells; blanching creates skins; crushing creates oil and meal. USDA is developing higher-value uses for shells and skins.

crops.name: Pecans
crops.byproducts: Shell and fiber streams are separated in processing; USDA studies shell compost and better shelling; oil/flour remain specialty or pilot pathways.

GA.role: The dominant peanut state and the largest state in USDA’s current five-state pecan table.
GA.ecosystem: The warm, sandy Coastal Plain: annual peanut rotations underground, pecan canopies above, shellers and food manufacturers woven through farm towns.

crops.name: Hazelnuts
crops.byproducts: Processors make meal, flour, oil and paste; Oregon State has designed shell-pyrolysis systems for heat, bio-oil and biochar.

OR.role: Oregon grows about 99% of the U.S. hazelnut crop. 2025 crop value more than doubled from 2024.
OR.ecosystem: The Willamette Valley: wet winters, mild summers, deep valley soils and a tree-crop culture rebuilt around disease-resistant cultivars.

crops.name: Pecans
crops.byproducts: Shell and fiber streams are separated in processing; USDA studies shell compost and better shelling; oil/flour remain specialty or pilot pathways.

NM.role: Pecans were New Mexico’s highest-valued USDA-listed crop in 2025.
NM.ecosystem: Arid river valleys where deep-rooted orchards are organized around irrigation, hot summers and high-value kernels grown against a desert horizon.

crops.byproducts: Shelling creates shells; blanching creates skins; crushing creates oil and meal. USDA is developing higher-value uses for shells and skins.

crops.byproducts: Shell and fiber streams are separated in processing; USDA studies shell compost and better shelling; oil/flour remain specialty or pilot pathways.

TX.role: A two-system nut state: peanuts across the southern Plains and pecans in river valleys and irrigated orchards.
TX.ecosystem: Texas links two geographies: annual peanut country on broad plains and long-lived pecan groves following water through hotter southern landscapes.

crops.name: Pecans
crops.byproducts: Shell and fiber streams are separated in processing; USDA studies shell compost and better shelling; oil/flour remain specialty or pilot pathways.

AZ.role: A compact, high-value desert pecan industry.
AZ.ecosystem: Heat, irrigation and desert soils produce a pecan economy whose limiting resource is not sunlight but water.

OK.role: A smaller but genuinely mixed peanut-and-pecan state.
OK.ecosystem: Southern Plains agriculture meets native and improved pecan systems.

AL.role: One of the core Southeastern peanut states.
AL.ecosystem: Warm Coastal Plain rotations where peanuts fit between cotton, corn and other annual crops.

FL.ecosystem: North Florida peanut country is part of the same warm Coastal Plain system that extends into Georgia and Alabama.

NC.ecosystem: Atlantic Coastal Plain fields connect growers to shellers and a long-established snack-peanut identity.

SC.ecosystem: Coastal Plain rotations continue the peanut landscape north and east from Georgia.

VA.ecosystem: A northern edge of the peanut belt with distinctive large-kernel market types.

AR.role: A smaller but high-yield peanut state.
AR.ecosystem: Peanuts fit into irrigated and rain-fed rotations in the lower Mississippi agricultural landscape.

MO.role: The northern/western edge of the USDA peanut reporting map.
MO.ecosystem: Peanut production here is a smaller extension of the southern field-crop system.

crops.name: Macadamias
crops.byproducts: Shells can fuel processing; husks can be mulched or composted; culled kernels make oil; press cake is being studied as feed.

HI.ecosystem: Island orchards under tropical sun: thick shells, rich oils and a processing chain where husk, shell, kernel and press cake can each become a product.
